chunks: From him, from Al-Barqi, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd, from Abdullah ibn Junadab, who narrates it up to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
The slave is the free man (who was freed), and his son is an Arab, and the son of his son is from himself (of his essence/lineage).

key_terms.الْجَلِيبُ: The one who is brought out (freed)
key_terms.عَرَبِيٌّ: Arab (often implying free/pure lineage in this context)

ai.seo_question: What is the status of the children and grandchildren of a freed slave in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Kafi, Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (AS) delineates the gradual elevation of social status across three generations of a freed slave, establishing a legal and spiritual hierarchy. The freed slave (mawla) retains a distinct identity as 'al-jalib' (the one brought out), his son is considered 'Arab' (free and of pure status), and his grandson is fully integrated as 'from himself,' signifying complete assimilation into the free community. This progression underscores the Shia emphasis on the dignity of manumission and the eventual erasure of servitude lineage in Islamic society.
